what_its_for: Torsemide is a 'water pill' (diuretic) that helps your body get rid of extra fluid and salt through your urine. It is used to treat swelling (edema) caused by heart failure, kidney disease, or liver disease. It is also used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Removing extra fluid helps reduce swelling in your legs, ankles, and feet, and makes it easier for your heart to work.
how_to_take: Take torsemide by mouth with or without food, usually once a day. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time each day. Because this medicine makes you urinate more often, try to take it in the morning so that frequent bathroom trips do not disturb your sleep at night. If you are on the extended-release tablet (Soaanz), swallow it whole — do not crush, chew, or split it.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how well the medicine is working. Common starting doses range from 5 mg to 20 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time if needed, up to a maximum of 200 mg per day in some cases. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose as scheduled. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store torsemide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid standing up too quickly, especially in the morning, as torsemide can lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can increase dizziness and lower blood pressure further. Be careful with salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay, since torsemide can change your potassium levels. Avoid spending too much time in the heat or exercising heavily without drinking enough fluids, as this can lead to dehydration. Talk to your doctor before taking other medications, including over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve), as these can reduce how well torsemide works and may harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe dizziness, fainting, or lightheadedness; muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat (signs of low potassium or sodium); signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, decreased urination, or feeling very weak; ringing in your ears or sudden hearing loss; swelling that gets worse or does not improve; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or chest pain or shortness of breath that is new or gets worse.
when_it_works: Torsemide starts working fairly quickly — you may notice increased urination within 1 hour of taking your first dose. The peak effect usually happens within 1 to 2 hours. For swelling, you may start to see and feel improvement within the first few days. For high blood pressure, it may take several weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well, because stopping it suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the effects of torsemide, especially dizziness and falls. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions and use caution. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Torsemide is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Breastfeeding: It is not known if torsemide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor will monitor you closely and may adjust your dose, as torsemide is used to treat these conditions but requires careful monitoring. Children: Torsemide is not typically recommended for children; talk to your doctor for guidance.
